ad10_pension.topic: Defined benefit to defined contribution: ERISA, PBGC, Studebaker, section 401(k), participation, balances, fees, auto-enrolment

claims.text: PBGC: Studebaker terminated its pension plan in 1963 and more than 8,500 workers at its South Bend plant lost some or all promised benefits; Ford signed ERISA on 2 September 1974, creating PBGC; first PBGC check $140.75 on 28 February 1975; about 926,000 retirees in more than 5,000 failed plans now paid by PBGC, another 428,000 to be paid; PBGC protects about 30 million in private DB plans
PBGC: at Studebaker about 3,600 retirees received full benefits; about 4,000 active employees received about 15% of expected benefits; thousands under 40 received nothing

DOL EBSA Table E7 active participants (thousands): 1975 DB 27,214 / DC 11,217; 1980 30,100/18,886; 1984 30,073/30,545 (first year DC exceeds DB); 1990 26,205/35,340; 2000 22,218/50,874; 2010 17,172/73,429; 2020 12,010/85,290; 2023 11,077/96,369. Plans 1975 DB 103,346; 1985 170,172; 2023 46,233 vs DC 790,610. Revised 2004 definition; counts are plan participants (a worker in two plans counted twice)

ICI 2006: Congress added section 401(k) in 1978 effective 1980; IRS proposed regulations 10 November 1981; CODAs since 1950s, approved by 1956 revenue ruling; ICI attributes the DB to DC shift mainly to industry composition, DB sponsors adding DC plans, new firms choosing DC; few firms replaced DB with 401(k) outright (ICI is the fund industry's trade association)

NAPA (Adams 2024): Revenue Act of 1978 signed 6 November 1978 by Carter, mainly tax cuts; added section 401(k); promoted by Rep. Barber Conable; 401(k)s were 'never intended (nor designed) to replace defined benefit pensions'; Benna/Johnson Companies story more nuanced

Vanguard HAS 2026 (2025 data, ~1,300 plans, 4.6m accounts): average balance $167,970, median $44,115; participation 83% participant-weighted; auto-enrolment plans 94% vs voluntary 64%; 61% of plans auto-enrol; participation by income under $15k 43%, $15-30k 57%, $30-50k 74%, $50-75k 86%, $100-150k 90%, $150k+ 95%; average deferral 7.6%, total contribution 12.1%; 13% have loans; 6% hardship withdrawals (median $1,900)

SCF 2025: 54.9% of families hold retirement accounts (54.3% in 2022); conditional median $106,000 (2025$); any plan (IRA/DC/DB) 65.1% of families with head 64 or younger; mean IRA/DC balance among holders 55-64 $670,200; DB plans held by about one-fourth of families
BLS NCS March 2026 private industry: access 72%, participation 52%; DC access 70% participation 49%; DB access 14% participation 9%; state and local government DB access 86%, participation rate 75%
ICI: 401(k) equity mutual fund asset-weighted expense ratio 0.76% (2000) to 0.26% (2024); target-date funds 0.67% (2008) to 0.29% (2024); industrywide equity average 0.40%

DOL fee illustration: $25,000, 35 years, 7% return, 0.5% vs 1.5% fees: $227,000 vs $163,000, 28% less; PolitiFact rated 'a third of savings to fees' Mostly False; Deloitte/ICI 2009 median all-in fee 0.72%
ICI: US retirement assets $51.2tn at 30 June 2026; IRAs $19.9tn; DC $15.0tn of which 401(k) $10.8tn; private DB $3.2tn; government DB $10.4tn; mutual funds hold 58% of 401(k) assets ($6.2tn)

SECURE 2.0 s.101 (IRC 414A): new 401(k)/403(b) plans established after 29 Dec 2022 must auto-enrol from plan years after 31 Dec 2024, 3-10% default rising 1 point a year to 10-15%; exempt employers with 10 or fewer employees, businesses under 3 years, church and government plans; final regs sent to OIRA 23 June 2026
AARP PPI: 17 states have passed legislation establishing auto-IRA programmes
DOL proposed rule 30 March 2026 creating a fiduciary safe harbour for alternative assets (private equity, crypto, real estate) in 401(k) plans, implementing an August 2025 executive order

ad10_socsec.topic: Social Security design, record, financing, cap, retirement age; old-age poverty; Elder Index; older workers

claims.text: AARP timeline: Act signed 14 Aug 1935; first monthly benefit 31 Jan 1940 ($22.54, Ida M. Fuller); 1950 first COLA (+77%); 1956 disability; 1961 age 62 for all; automatic COLA signed 1 July 1972 from 1975; SSI Oct 1972; 1983 amendments signed 20 April 1983 (FRA 65 to 67; up to 50% taxable); 2026 Trustees Report 9 June 2026

SSA: 1983 amendments signed 20 April 1983 on recommendations of the National Commission on Social Security Reform; FRA raised in two stages to 67 by 2027, first affecting those born 1938; benefits taxable up to half above $25,000/$32,000 from 1984; COLA delayed six months; employee rate schedule accelerated to 7.65% by 1990 (incl. HI); new federal employees covered from 1 Jan 1984
CRS 2023: 90% of covered earnings taxable in 1982 (goal of 1977 amendments) vs 81% in 2021; about 6% of workers earn above the base

NAPA 14 Oct 2026: 2027 COLA 3.6%; taxable maximum $184,500 (2026) to $192,300 (2027); average monthly benefit about $2,088 (2026), about $2,163 from January 2027; more than 76 million receive Social Security or SSI

CRS on 2026 Trustees: OASI depleted Q4 2032; OASDI Q3 2034; then about 83% payable falling to 65% by 2100; DI not depleted; deficit 4.42% of payroll vs 3.82%, due to lower fertility (1.90 to 1.75), lower immigration, and P.L. 119-21 reducing income from taxation of benefits; 2025 income: payroll tax 91.3%, benefit taxation 4.0%, interest 4.8%
AARP Foundation (Census data): SPM poverty 65+ 15.4% in 2025, up from 9.4% in 2020; over 10 million older adults below SPM; LeadingAge: 12.7% in 2019; men 13.7%, women 16.8% (2025)

UMass Boston 2019 Elder Index: 50% of single older adults and 23% of older couples had incomes below the Elder Index; 18.2% of singles below poverty and 32.1% 'in the gap'; average Elder Index $25,416 single renter, $36,204 couple (2019)
UMass Boston 2026: Massachusetts 60% of older single adults below Elder Index (2nd among states), couples 27% (5th)

Pew 2023: 19% of adults 65+ working vs 11% in 1987 and 18% in early 1960s; 75+ 9% vs 4% in 1987; ~11m older workers; 45% of employed older adults consider themselves retired (Fed survey); BLS projects 65+ participation 19% to 21% by 2032
